headline_marked: Opposition MPs [[walk out of parliament]] over constitutional amendment committee
headline: Opposition MPs walk out of parliament over constitutional amendment committee
summary: Lawmakers reject the treasury bench's move to form a special committee to amend the constitution in line with the July Charter.
details: Opposition MPs walked out of parliament after rejecting the treasury bench's proposal to form a Special Parliamentary Committee on Amending the Constitution. The move was intended to align the constitution with the July Charter.

Chief Whip Nurul Islam Moni proposed 12 members for the 17-member committee, which was to be headed by Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed. Minutes after the names were presented, Opposition Leader Shafiqur Rahman announced the walkout.

Shafiqur Rahman stated that his party had opposed the committee from the start, arguing that it contradicts the will of the people. He highlighted that a 68.6 percent vote in a referendum had endorsed the implementation of the July Charter.

The opposition maintains that the July Charter's 48 proposals for reform should be implemented through a Constitution Reform Council, rather than a special parliamentary committee. They argue that ignoring the public mandate is unacceptable.

Earlier, Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman noted that the ruling party had prepared a list of members including representatives from BNP and other opposition parties. He mentioned that the opposition holds 26 percent of the seats in parliament.

The July National Charter, drafted by the National Consensus Commission, outlines 48 proposals for constitutional reform. While some parties favor full implementation through a Reform Council, the BNP has submitted notes of dissent on several key provisions.

headline_marked: Weather alerts: [[HSC exams to continue]] despite heavy rain and flooding
headline: Weather alerts: HSC exams to continue despite heavy rain and flooding
summary: The Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee says most centres remain fit for use, though exams in Chattogram have been postponed.
details: The HSC and equivalent examinations will continue in most parts of the country despite adverse weather. The Bangladesh Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee stated that most centres remain suitable for use.
Approximately 1,270,583 examinees are sitting for the exams at 2,697 centres across all education boards. The committee acknowledged concerns from students and guardians regarding the heavy rain.
However, exams under the Chattogram Education Board have been postponed until July 16, as several centres were affected by flooding and students could not safely reach the venues.

The committee noted that repeated postponements could disrupt the academic calendar, university admissions, and result publications. They stated that postponing all boards due to issues in one board is not practical.
In Cumilla, students at Cumilla Government Women’s College managed to take their exams with support from guardians and local officials despite unexpected adverse weather.
The committee stressed that student safety is the highest priority. If a natural disaster seriously threatens exams in any area, the local deputy commissioner will make immediate decisions.
caption:
1.2 million students are battling floods and rain to take their HSC exams. The board says most centres are still fit for use.

The HSC and equivalent examinations will continue in most parts of the country despite adverse weather. The Bangladesh Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee stated that most centres remain suitable for use.

Approximately 1,270,583 examinees are sitting for the exams at 2,697 centres across all education boards. The committee acknowledged concerns from students and guardians regarding the heavy rain.

However, exams under the Chattogram Education Board have been postponed until July 16, as several centres were affected by flooding and students could not safely reach the venues.

The committee noted that repeated postponements could disrupt the academic calendar, university admissions, and result publications. They stated that postponing all boards due to issues in one board is not practical.

In Cumilla, students at Cumilla Government Women’s College managed to take their exams with support from guardians and local officials despite unexpected adverse weather.

The committee stressed that student safety is the highest priority. If a natural disaster seriously threatens exams in any area, the local deputy commissioner will make immediate decisions.
